Many streetlights have a photocell light detector on them to turn them on when it gets dark and off again in daylight. I had an 'event' that was most definitely strange.

Back in 1991 I was travelling to the Isle of Skye with my wife and daughter and was a mile or two south of a place called the Kyle of Lochalsh. It was a trip I had undertaken a number of times and so I knew the road quite well, especially since there is only one road at that section.

At that time in order to get to the Isle of Skye you had to catch a 5 minute ferry from the Kyle but there was talk of building the bridge that's there now.

Anyway, on this single bit of road that I knew quite well I suddenly came upon an unexpected mini roundabout. It looked as if roadworks were ongoing with traffic cones all over the place and traffic lights just before the roundabout. They turned to green and as I began to move off I noticed that to my left was a road bridge which was 'fed' from the mini roundabout but a fog had developed out of nowhere so all I could see was the road disappearing up into it.

Thinking they must have brought the build schedule forward I took the left turn from the roundabout and headed towards the bridge. The fog thickened so I didn't really accelerate to more than 20mph and began to go up this new road onto the bridge, maybe about 100 yards or so. By now the fog is so thick I'm struggling to see much more than a couple of car lengths in front of me and that's when I noticed the bridge just seemed to end over the water.

Now I hadn't seen any signs saying the road was incomplete or anything and the road I was on was a crisp, new one with gleaming white lines and the like but I didn't like the way it just seemed to disappear in the fog, so I stopped, turned the car around and headed back down to the roundabout. As I did so the fog evaporated and by the time I was back on the road to the Kyle it was a bright, clear day again.

Fast forward a few days and on the way home I looked for the bridge to see how far along the build was as I came to the area with the mini roundabout and there was nothing. Just the single road that had always been there. No mini roundabout, no roadworks and definitely no bridge.
